Package org.ujorm.orm

Interface Crud<D,V>

Type Parameters:
D - The domain class type (e.g., Entity or Record)
V - The primary key class type
All Known Implementing Classes:
EntityManager.CrudImpl
public interface Crud<D,V>
Interface for standard CRUD (Create, Read, Update, Delete) operations.

This interface provides a comprehensive set of methods to interact with the database, ranging from single-entity operations to highly optimized, memory-efficient batch processing using Java Streams. It is designed to fully support both traditional mutable JavaBeans and modern immutable objects (like Java Records).

  • Method Details

    • insertBatch

      long insertBatch(@NotNull @NotNull Stream<D> domains, @Nullable @Nullable Consumer<D> onInserted)
      Inserts a stream of domain objects into the database using JDBC batching.

      Performance & Memory: The stream is processed sequentially and eagerly. Entities are chunked into small batches, ensuring minimal memory footprint even when processing millions of records.

      Parameters:
      domains - A stream of entities to be inserted. If a parallel stream is provided, it will be forced to sequential execution to guarantee JDBC thread safety.
      onInserted - An optional callback invoked for each successfully inserted entity. This is the recommended way to retrieve newly generated primary keys, especially for immutable objects (Records) where a new instance is yielded.
      Returns:
      The total number of successfully inserted rows.

    • insertBatch

      D[] insertBatch(@NotNull @NotNull D... domains)
      Inserts an array (or varargs) of domain objects using batching support.

      The method processes the items and updates the array elements in-place with generated identifiers. If the domain objects are immutable (like Java Records), new instances are created and placed back into the corresponding array indices.

      CRITICAL WARNING: Always capture and use the returned array! If you pass elements directly via varargs (creating an implicit array), the method replaces the instances inside that temporary array. You will lose all references to the updated entities with generated keys if you ignore the return value.

      Parameters:
      domains - The array or varargs of entities to insert.
      Returns:
      The original array containing the inserted entities, updated with generated identifiers.

    • insert

      D insert(@NotNull D domain)
      Inserts a single domain object into the database.
      Parameters:
      domain - The domain object to be inserted (either a mutable JavaBean or an immutable Record).
      Returns:
      The domain object populated with the newly generated primary key. For mutable objects, this is typically the same instance passed as the parameter. For immutable Records, a completely new instance is returned.
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - If no generated ID value could be retrieved from the database.

    • insertOrUpdate

      long insertOrUpdate(@NotNull @NotNull Stream<D> domains, @Nullable @Nullable Consumer<D> onInserted, CharSequence... properties)
      Processes a stream of domain objects and decides dynamically whether to insert or update each entity.

      The decision is based on the primary key: if the primary key is empty (null or zero), the entity is inserted. Otherwise, it is updated.

      Performance: Stream operations are evaluated sequentially. To ensure optimal memory usage, entities are grouped into small batches for both INSERT and UPDATE statements under the hood.

      Parameters:
      domains - A stream of entities to be processed.
      onInserted - An optional callback invoked only for newly inserted entities. Useful for capturing the assigned primary keys.
      properties - Optional list of specific property names to update (applies to UPDATE operations only). If empty, all columns except the primary key are updated.
      Returns:
      The total number of rows affected (both inserted and updated).

    • update

      long update(@NotNull @NotNull Stream<D> domains, CharSequence... properties)
      Updates a stream of domain objects efficiently using JDBC batching.

      Note: This method executes a full update for each entity based on the provided properties. It does not check for actual changes. For optimized, partial updates, see updateChanged(Stream).

      Parameters:
      domains - A stream of domain objects to update. Evaluated sequentially.
      properties - An optional list of specific property (column) names to update for all entities in the batch. If empty, all columns (excluding the primary key) are updated.
      Returns:
      The total number of rows affected by the batch update execution.

    • updateChanged

      default <D2 extends SnapshotProvider<D2>> long updateChanged(@NotNull D2 domain)
      Updates a single domain object optimally by detecting actual modifications.

      Important: The entity must implement the SnapshotProvider interface. Only the columns that have actually changed (compared to the entity's internal snapshot) are included in the SQL UPDATE statement. If no changes are detected, the DB hit is skipped.

      Type Parameters:
      D2 - The type of the domain object, bounded by SnapshotProvider.
      Parameters:
      domain - The domain object to update.
      Returns:
      The number of affected rows (1 if updated, 0 if skipped due to no changes).
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - If the entity is missing a saved snapshot.

    • updateChanged

      default <D2 extends SnapshotProvider<D2>> long updateChanged(@NotNull @NotNull D2... domains)
      Updates an array of domain objects optimally using batching and collision detection.

      Note: It is highly recommended to disable auto-commit (connection.setAutoCommit(false)) for transactional safety and performance during batch operations.

      Important: Entities must implement the SnapshotProvider interface. The underlying SQL statements are dynamically generated and batched based on the specific columns changed in each entity.

      Type Parameters:
      D2 - The type of the domain object, bounded by SnapshotProvider.
      Parameters:
      domains - An array or varargs of domain objects to update.
      Returns:
      The total number of rows updated in the database.
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - If any entity is missing a saved snapshot.
      IllegalArgumentException - If the array contains nulls or objects of an invalid type.

    • updateChanged

      <D2 extends SnapshotProvider<D2>> long updateChanged(@NotNull @NotNull Stream<D2> domains)
      Updates a stream of domain objects optimally using batching and collision detection.

      Note: It is highly recommended to disable auto-commit (connection.setAutoCommit(false)) for transactional safety and performance during batch operations.

      Important: Entities must implement the SnapshotProvider interface. The internal engine dynamically groups and batches entities that share the exact same modification pattern (same changed columns), maximizing JDBC batching efficiency while skipping entities with zero changes.

      Type Parameters:
      D2 - The type of the domain object, bounded by SnapshotProvider.
      Parameters:
      domains - A stream of domain objects to process.
      Returns:
      The total number of rows updated in the database.
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - If any entity is missing a saved snapshot.
      IllegalArgumentException - If the stream contains nulls or objects of an invalid type.
